questions.prompt: Next.js 16 shows more granular prefetch requests in dev tools. What should a senior engineer check first?

options.label: Disable prefetching because more requests always means worse performance.
Compare total transferred bytes, navigation latency, and origin load.
Force every route to dynamic rendering.

questions.explanation: Enhanced routing can reduce total transfer while changing request shape. Measure outcomes, not only request count.

questions.prompt: Fill the performance target for streamed routes.
questions.template: Streaming works best when the first response is a useful {{blank}}, not a blank page.
questions.explanation: A useful shell gives users structure while dynamic content resolves.

items.label: Name the user job and critical path
Measure shell, dynamic content, and navigation timing
Protect with browser and build checks

questions.explanation: Performance work should optimize a measured user path and protect it from regression.

questions.prompt: Match each Next.js 16 feature to the performance lever.

pairs.match: faster dev and production build feedback
deduplicated layout and incremental prefetch payloads
less repeated server work for safe shared output

questions.explanation: Each feature affects a different part of the performance system.

options.label: Wrap only the slow personalized panel and keep navigation stable.
Wrap the entire page in one fallback because one widget is slow.
Use stable dimensions for a delayed analytics chart.

questions.explanation: A broad fallback throws away the useful shell and makes streaming feel like blocking.

questions.prompt: Order a Turbopack migration review for a customized app.

items.label: Run dev and production builds under Turbopack
Exercise routes that depend on custom bundling
Document opt-out only if parity fails

questions.explanation: Faster defaults still need compatibility review when the app has custom bundler assumptions.
